prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on what you need (individual vs family, budget, marketplace/ACA vs private/short‑term, in‑person help, ongoing service). I can find local brokers for you, but first a couple quick questions to narrow it down:

- Do you need an ACA/Marketplace plan (with premium tax credits) or a private/short‑term plan?
- Individual or family coverage? Any special needs (prescriptions, chronic conditions, preferred doctors)?
- Do you want an in‑person/local broker in Kansas City or are you fine with a phone/online broker?
- What’s your ZIP code (so I can find nearby options)?

If you’d rather get started now, here’s how to pick a great broker for a self‑employed person and what to ask them:

What to look for
- Independent broker (not tied to a single carrier) so you get unbiased comparisons.
- Experience with ACA/individual market and with self‑employed clients.
- Licensed in Missouri (verify via Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance).
- Good recent reviews and willingness to provide references.
- Clear explanation of fees/commission (many individual plan brokers are paid by carriers; confirm there will be no surprise client fees).
- Offers ongoing support (claims help, renewals, mid‑year changes).

Key questions to ask a broker
- Are you independent or captive to one carrier?
- How many individual/ACA enrollments have you handled in the last year?
- Do you help with estimating tax credits and comparing net monthly cost?
- Will you help with provider/network confirmation and prescription coverage?
- What are your fees, if any? How are you compensated?
- Will you assist with claims or appeals if problems arise?

Places to search/contact
- Local independent insurance agencies (search Google for “independent health insurance broker Kansas City MO”).
- National online brokers that specialize in self‑employed/individual plans (if you prefer online).
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance to verify licensing.
- Kansas City Area chapter of the National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) for local reputable brokers.

If you share ZIP code and whether you want ACA vs private coverage and in‑person vs online service, I’ll pull a short list of well‑rated local brokers and contact options.
